Pit gain is zero, so influx height and gradient are not calculated.
SIDPP is zero. If a float is in the string, SIDPP must be read by bumping the float before KMW can be trusted.

The string is tapered: the straight-line schedule runs up to 21 psi below the hydrostatic section points (bottom-hole pressure dips below formation pressure by that much while KMW goes down the string). Compare with the section points.
Kill mud weight is at or above the shoe LOT/FIT EMW. Losses at the shoe are expected once KMW is in the annulus above the shoe. Stop and escalate.
SICP is at or above MAASP for the current mud weight. The shoe may already be at risk. Escalate before circulating.

A straight line from ICP to FCP would hold up to 25 psi more drill pipe pressure than the section schedule. That adds the same amount to bottom-hole pressure and to the shoe load.
A straight line from ICP to FCP would run up to 14 psi below the section schedule (underbalanced). Use the section schedule.
Influx height is measured along hole. In an inclined bottom section the vertical height is shorter, so the gradient is less reliable.
Well MD exceeds TVD by more than 2 percent. The straight-line schedule overstates drill pipe pressure in a deviated well. Consider deviated mode.

cases.error: Shoe MD is deeper than the well MD (TD). Check the shoe and well depths.
cases.name: err_shoe_below_td

cases.error: Pump output must be greater than zero. A zero pump output makes every stroke count infinite.
cases.name: err_zero_pump

cases.error: Drill string section lengths add to 9140.0 ft but the well MD is 10000.0 ft. They must match (bit on bottom).
cases.name: err_string_length

cases.error: Well TVD cannot be greater than well MD.
cases.name: err_tvd_gt_md

cases.error: Pit gain is larger than the whole annular volume. Check the pit gain and annular capacities.
cases.name: err_gain_too_big

cases.error: Enter the LOT/FIT as an EMW, or as a surface leak-off pressure plus the test mud weight.
cases.name: err_no_lot

cases.name: err_lot_below_mw
